THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 10.01.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:1862 Anwarsha.

This Bail Application is filed under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.
2. Petitioners are the 1st and 2nd accused in Crime No.496 of 2024 of Haripad Police Station.

The above case is registered against the petitioners alleging offences punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860 and also under Sections 3 and 9 of the Kerala Prohibition of Charging Exorbitant Interest Act, 2012.

entities.text: Kerala Prohibition of Charging Exorbitant Interest Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The prosecution case is that the petitioners with dishonest intention, induced the defacto complainant and to get unlawful gain to them, made her believe that they are the Directors of AUX NIDHI Limited, 2025:KER:1862 a financial institution and they gave housing loan on security of Title Deed and that the loan amount would be repaid only after one year, after construction of the house.

The petitioners created Sale Deed for the property of the husband of the defacto complainant under the guise of loan related documents and obtained her signature in the fraudulently created Sale Deed.

There after during the period from 19.07.2022 till 13.12.2022, they transferred a total amount of Rs.16,55,600/- on different dates from the account of the petitioners to the account of the defacto complainant, maintained with the South Indian Bank.
Thus the petitioners cheated the defacto complainant by not giving the entire loan of Rs.40,00,000/- and forged a Sale Deed in order to charge excessive interest on the amount availed by her as loan.
The case is registered based on private complaint filed before the Jurisdictional Court, which was forwarded to the Investigating Officer.
4. Heard counsel for the petitioners and the Public Prosecutor.
5. Counsel appearing for the petitioners submitted that even if the entire allegations are accepted no offence is made out.
The counsel submitted that Annexure A3 is a registered Sale Deed.
Subsequently, a Sale Agreement was also executed.
The counsel submitted that even if the entire allegations are accepted, the remedy of the defacto complainant is to approach the competent Civil Court.
6. Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.

sentences.text: 7. This Court considered the contention of the petitioners and the Public Prosecutor.
After hearing both sides, I am of the considered opinion that the prosecution can prove the case through oral or documentary evidence.
No custodial interrogation of the petitioners is necessary in the facts and circumstances of 2025:KER:1862 the case.
The petitioners can be directed to co-operate with the investigation.
8. Moreover, it is a well accepted principle that the bail is the rule and the jail is the exception.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Chidambaram.

P v Directorate of Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870],
after considering all the earlier judgments, observed that, the basic jurisprudence relating to bail remains the same inasmuch as the grant of bail is the rule and refusal is the exception so as to ensure that the accused has the opportunity of securing fair trial.

entities.text: P v Directorate of Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. Recently the Apex Court in Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
considered the point in detail.

entities.text: Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant paragraph of the above judgment is extracted hereunder.
"12. We may note that personal liberty is an important aspect of our constitutional mandate.

The occasion to arrest an accused during investigation arises when custodial 2025:KER:1862 investigation becomes necessary or it is a heinous crime or where there is a possibility of influencing the witnesses or accused may abscond.
Merely because an arrest can be made because it is lawful does not mandate that arrest must be made.
A distinction must be made between the existence of the power to arrest and the justification for exercise of it.
(Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189: (1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981))

entities.text: Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189: (1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If arrest is made routine, it can cause incalculable harm to the reputation and self-esteem of a person.

If the Investigating Officer has no reason to believe that the accused will abscond or disobey summons and has, in fact,
throughout cooperated with the investigation we fail to appreciate why there should be a compulsion on the officer to arrest the accused."

In Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961], the Apex Court observed that even if the allegation is one of grave economic offence, it is not a rule that bail should be denied in every case.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Considering the dictum laid down in the above decision and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this Bail Application is allowed with the following directions:
1.
The petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer within two weeks from today and shall undergo interrogation.

2. After interrogation, if the Investigating Officer propose to arrest the petitioners,they shall be released on bail on executing a bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand 2025:KER:1862 only) with two solvent sureties Anwarsha.

3 each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the arresting officer concerned.
3. The petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer for interrogation as and when required.
The petitioners shall co-

operate with the investigation and shall not, directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
4. Petitioners shall not leave India without permission of the jurisdictional Court.
5. Petitioners shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which 2025:KER:1862 they are accused, or suspected, of the commission of which they are suspected.

6. Needless to mention, it would be well within the powers of the investigating officer to investigate the matter and, if necessary, to effect recoveries on the information, if any, given by the petitioners even while the petitioners are on bail as laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sushila Aggarwal v.
State (NCT of Delhi) and another [2020 (1) KHC 663].
7.

Sushila Aggarwal v.
State (NCT of Delhi) and another [2020 (1) KHC 663]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any of the above conditions are violated by the petitioners, the jurisdictional Court can cancel the bail in accordance to law, even though the bail is granted by this Court.
The 2025:KER:1862 prosecution and the victim are at liberty to approach the jurisdictional Court to cancel the bail, if any of the above conditions are violated.

Sd/-
P.V.KUNHIKRISHNAN JUDGE AMR Anwarsha.
